summary:
Adıyaman Province stands under the national framework of Türkiye. The provisions that govern a trans visitor's exposure in the province are national, and the source inventory contains no Adıyaman-specific carve-out from any of them: no local policing practice, no local facility rule and no local variation in the documents regime is documented for the province.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in Türkiye since 1858 under the Ottoman penal code, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, when gender reassignment surgery became legal. These provisions apply countrywide, including in Adıyaman Province.

A leaked draft omnibus justice reform, described by Human Rights Watch as the '11th Judicial Package' and reported on 29 October 2025, would enable criminal charges against LGBT people in Türkiye. Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades; Istanbul activists held a press conference against it on 28 October 2025. The draft is national-level and would apply countrywide if adopted, with no province-specific provisions.

Türkiye has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military. These provisions are countrywide, with no Adıyaman-specific content.

Same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition in Türkiye: marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unavailable, and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals. A trans visitor in what would be locally classed as a same-sex relationship therefore has no recognised partner status in the province.
tangentialFactors: The 11th Judicial Package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025 is a draft, not enacted law; whether it has since passed is unresolved in the sources. Istanbul activists' press conference of 28 October 2025 indicates organised national opposition to the package, but no Adıyaman-based activism or response is documented in the inventory.
localsOnly: Residents of Adıyaman Province live under the same national provisions as visitors: same-sex conduct is legal, legal gender change has been available since 1988, no comprehensive discrimination protection exists on sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex relationships carry no legal recognition. No province-specific resident-facing rule, protection mechanism or local institution is documented in the inventory.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since Human Rights Watch's 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

The inventory contains no Adıyaman-specific data on policing practice, detention conditions, facility access, hate-crime incidents or local civil-society capacity; the absence of such records is not evidence that none exist.

Enforcement patterns for the national provisions within Adıyaman Province are not sourced.
